skill.name: character-creation-studio
skill.description: Use this Chinese-language workflow to design original characters and casts, write English prompts for GPT Image, and prepare character assets for video production. An image tool is required to render the assets.
skill.summary: Design characters, record approved visual traits, and reuse them in prompts for turnarounds, expression sheets, and production handoffs.
skill.author: 287523023qq-hue

security_audit.summary: All 66 static alerts were false positives: manual installation examples, Markdown formatting, and readable documentation accounted for the matches. No evidence of runtime shell execution, unauthorized data transfer, or prompt injection was found. The README misstates redistribution rights and overstates image consistency, which can affect marketplace distribution and purchase decisions.

remediation.issue: The MIT badge conflicts with the repository license.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the badge with an accurate custom-license notice. Obtain written permission before mirroring or repackaging the skill, or link to the source without redistributing it.

remediation.issue: The promotional showcase claims absolute turnaround consistency.
remediation.suggestion: Describe the showcased result as an example, not a guarantee. Explain that users must inspect generated images against the approved reference before delivery.

semantic_findings.title: MIT Badge Conflicts With Redistribution Terms
semantic_findings.description: The README displays a License: MIT badge, but the governing license prohibits redistribution of the package or its excerpts. A marketplace could mistake the badge for permission to mirror or repackage the files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The badge links directly to license text that expressly forbids both paid and free redistribution. The conflict does not depend on interpreting author intent.

semantic_findings.title: Promotional Claim Overstates Character Consistency
semantic_findings.description: The README promotes paid installation and advertises 100% stable turnarounds in its showcase. The skill states that no model guarantees complete consistency and requires visual review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The showcase gives an absolute stability figure without a measured scope. The documented acceptance process treats visual consistency as a result to verify for each asset.

content.value_statement: Generated character images can change faces, proportions, or costume details across views. This workflow records approved traits and uses them to guide new images and check the results.
actual_capabilities: Turn a short brief into a character concept with distinct silhouettes, materials, and identifying details.
Plan a cast with shared setting rules and visible differences in height, shape, color, and props.
Write English prompts that separate fixed identity traits from view, pose, lighting, and style.
Record approved reference traits in a versioned lock record, including feature counts and the character's left or right side.
Specify turnarounds, expression sheets, portraits, and detail sheets with checks for unwanted changes.
Prepare a video handoff checklist and a reusable character description from the current character version.
limitations: The skill writes prompts and specifications. It needs a separate image tool to render or edit images.
It cannot guarantee visual consistency or verify images it cannot inspect.
It prepares character assets for video production but does not write or generate video shots.
The free edition includes sample library entries and test results. Complete style rows, named species catalogs, and detailed test logs are not bundled.

use_cases.title: Develop an illustration protagonist
use_cases.description: Turn a short character idea into a distinct silhouette, a few identifying traits, and a prompt for a neutral master image.

use_cases.title: Plan a game faction
use_cases.description: Define shared materials and faction marks, then compare each member by height, silhouette, color, and signature prop.

use_cases.title: Prepare a video character handoff
use_cases.description: List required reference images, approved traits, and known weak points so a video team can reuse the same character.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a character and prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Start with a one-sentence brief.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a character from [one-sentence brief]. Give me three visible identity traits and one English GPT Image prompt. Do not generate an image.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a distinct cast
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Create a cast for one setting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three characters for [setting] with these roles: [roles]. Define their shared materials and visual style. Give each a distinct silhouette, height, dominant color, and prop.

prompt_templates.title: Derive a three-view sheet
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Work from an approved master image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [master image] and [lock record] to write a same-scale front, side, and back turnaround prompt. Change only the viewing angle. Label any unseen costume detail as inferred.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a versioned handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Prepare references for a downstream video team.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [approved master], [lock record], and [available sheets] to prepare a character handoff. Include the current version, a reusable identity description, and the recommended first-frame reference. Mark missing assets and unverified traits.

output_examples.input: Design a greenhouse maintenance robot. Give me the master image prompt only.
output: Identity: A compact greenhouse robot with one amber lens, a green tool apron, and a square watering tank.
Master image prompt: Show the full robot from the front, standing neutrally against a light gray background under even, soft light.
Rendering style: Painted metal and visible canvas texture. No lettering.

output_examples.input: Prepare a turnaround brief for this approved courier. The rear view is not visible in the reference.
output: Locked traits: Short black curls, two brass coat clasps, and a canvas pouch at the character's left hip.
Turnaround brief: Show front, side, and rear views at the same scale, with the same pose and lighting.
Unverified: Rear coat construction. Continue the visible fabric and mark the rear seam as inferred until approved.

best_practices: Approve a neutral master image before recording fixed traits or requesting new views.
Assign each reference image one role, such as face, clothing, pose, or rendering style.
Review each rendered image against the lock record and mark obscured details as unverified.
anti_patterns: Changing the face, outfit, and framing in one edit makes it hard to identify why the result changed.
Using an unapproved exploration image as the master can introduce traits that conflict with the final design.
Marking a prompt-only result as visually verified claims an inspection that did not happen.

faq.question: Can I use the skill without an image tool?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft character concepts, prompts, and checklists. It cannot render images or verify visual consistency without seeing the images.

faq.question: Which image tools does the workflow cover?
faq.answer: GPT Image is the main production target. Midjourney is optional for exploration, and separate notes cover still-image style testing in Grok Imagine.

faq.question: What is a lock record?
faq.answer: It records the approved master image, fixed visual traits, permitted changes, and details that still need verification.

faq.question: Can it work from an existing character image?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the base image and specify what to preserve and what may change. The workflow also lets you assign a separate role to each reference.

faq.question: Does it produce a finished video?
faq.answer: No. It prepares character sheets, a reusable identity description, and handoff notes for a separate video workflow.

faq.question: What is available in the free edition?
faq.answer: It includes the main workflow, prompt templates, sample style and species entries, and a worked example. Complete catalogs and test logs belong to the paid edition.
